headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surfaces can ingest untrusted content, while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and provides no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces and can ingest external metadata, so prompt-like content could reach its context. The zoomcamp profile is a non-runnable course with no shared channel or parser controls, so the pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests attacker-controlled metadata or webhook payloads as instructions
IF the zoomcamp content is manually copied into OpenMetadata or another parser without sanitization
mitigations: Disable or restrict MCP/webhook ingestion for untrusted sources
Add provenance labels to imported content
Require human review before treating imported text as instructions
Use a separate workspace for course material
requires-engineering: add content-type filtering and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: The zoomcamp profile shows no data classes touched and no egress, while OpenMetadata touches governance and lineage metadata and can call APIs. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or sensitive data flow between them, so leakage is possible only through unusual operator setup and the blast radius appears limited.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive files from the zoomcamp workspace into OpenMetadata-managed metadata
IF OpenMetadata is configured to sync those files or metadata to external APIs
mitigations: Keep course files and OpenMetadata catalogs in separate directories
Avoid importing secrets or personal data into the catalog
Review outbound API destinations in OpenMetadata
Use a throwaway test dataset
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and mutable API/MCP interactions, but the zoomcamp profile is not runnable and has no write surfaces. Because only one agent has operational write capability, there is no meaningful same-resource write conflict documented here.
conditions: IF the zoomcamp repository is mounted as a writable shared workspace with OpenMetadata-managed files
IF both agents are configured to modify the same external resource through APIs or MCP
mitigations: Do not mount the same directory writable in both systems
Assign separate service accounts
Avoid concurrent edits to shared metadata objects
Use manual change approval for shared resources
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can act on metadata and lineage information, so if it consumes outputs derived from the zoomcamp material without verification, errors can propagate into catalogs or downstream actions. The zoomcamp profile itself is static course content, so the risk is inferred from the interaction rather than directly observed; uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata imports course-derived metadata without validation
IF downstream workflows trust imported lineage or governance fields as authoritative
mitigations: Add a verification step before import
Mark imported fields as untrusted until reviewed
Limit automation on newly imported metadata
Sample-check lineage and governance records
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge, which can create retention or residency concerns if regulated data is stored there. The zoomcamp profile has no data classes touched and no residency indicators, so only OpenMetadata is relevant; the other agent is not cited because it contributes no compliance surface here.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into OpenMetadata without matching retention or residency controls
IF the operator uses OpenMetadata to store subject-identifiable metadata
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in the catalog
Review retention settings before import
Restrict access to governance metadata
Document data residency for connected APIs
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
